newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour wins by-election, Major govt in minority.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour wins by-election, Major govt in minority.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party won a key by-election in north west England on Thursday, pushing Prime Minister John Major's Conservative government into a parliamentary minority, officials announced.

Labour's Ben Chapman won the seat of Wirral South with a majority of 7,888, reversing a Conservative majority of 8,183 at the last election in 1992. The swing to Labour was a huge 18 percent, mirroring Labour's national poll lead of 20 percent.

The seat fell vacant with the death of Conservative member of parliament Barry Porter in December. The by-election was seen as a key test for Major, who must call a nationwide election by May at the latest. His favoured date is believed to be May 1.
The Conservatives have come back before from by-election defeats to win national elections, but no government in recent history has overcome such a deficit in only a few months.

The defeat leaves Major with 322 parliamentary seats, one less than all other parties combined, increasing his reliance on minority parties like Northern Ireland's Ulster Unionists. But the Ulster Unionists made clear on Thursday they would not bring down the government to force an early election.
